_about: DayForge getting-started tour. Each slide: title, text, optional shot (a screenshot name from shots.py) with points [[pin number on that screenshot, what it does], ...], or a diagram [[title, detail], ...]. Built by guides/lib/build.py; keep wording plain and match the app's labels exactly.
intro: A quick walk through the screens with real screenshots. Pick the path that fits you; you can take the other one after.

done.user: That's the whole day-to-day loop. Replay this tour any time from ⋮ › Getting started tour, or open the full guide for every detail.
done.admin: Those are the owner's jobs. The full guide's Admin section has the step-by-step details and a troubleshooting table.

user.label: Everyday use
user.blurb: Planning your day, notes, routines and calendar export.

slides.title: Your day on one screen
slides.text: Everything happens on the dashboard: pick a day, see it hour by hour, and keep tasks without a time to one side.
points: Forecast: the next 7 days. Tap a day to plan it.
Timeline: the selected day, 5 AM to 11 PM.
Tray: tasks that don't have a time yet.

slides.title: Capture in seconds
slides.text: Type or paste several tasks at once. Each line becomes its own task in the tray.
points: One task per line.
Personal or Work, for every line.
Add to tray.

slides.title: Give tasks a time
slides.text: Schedule from the tray. If you move something by mistake, an Undo button appears for a few seconds.
points: Tap a task, tick “Give this a date and time block”, then pick the date and time. Easiest on a phone.
Or drag the handle onto the hour you want.

slides.title: Work through the day
slides.text: Blocks are as tall as the task is long, and overlapping tasks sit side by side.
points: Tick it done.
Tap the name to open its details.
Drag to another hour, or onto the tray to unschedule it.

slides.title: Everything about a task
slides.text: Open any task for its details. Changes to an existing task save on their own.
points: Record a voice note.
Attach any file, with a label.
Duration and end time keep each other in sync.
Repeat daily, or weekly on the days you pick.

slides.title: Keep things in view
slides.text: Pinned holds reminders that don't belong at a particular time, like a deadline next month.
points: Type a reminder, then tap Pin.
Tap it to open it; tick it when it's done.

slides.title: Routines
slides.text: Save a set of tasks, like a morning routine, and drop it onto any day already timed.
points: Name a routine and tap Create.
Apply to day adds its items to the selected date.
Add items with a time and length.

slides.title: Notes for everything else
slides.text: Jot down what isn't a task yet. Tap the box and today's date starts the note; dashes and stars build an outline as you type.
points: The capture box.
Labels: create and manage categories.
Tap a label to see only those notes.
Pin a note to the top.

slides.title: Turn notes into tasks
slides.text: When a note is ready, convert it. The title becomes the task and the bullets become its notes.
points: Convert to task sends it to the tray.
Color tints the card.
Labels: tick on or off, or type a new one.

slides.title: Send it to your calendar
slides.text: Export a day or a week as a file that Google Calendar, Outlook or Apple Calendar can import.
points: This day, or this week.
Personal, Work, or both.
Download .ics.

slides.title: The menu
slides.text: The ⋮ button at the end of the top bar.
points: Refresh app loads the newest version after an update.
Replay this tour any time.
The full guide: every screen and setting.

slides.title: What's new
slides.text: After an update, this card shows what changed since you last looked, once per account. You only see the changes that apply to you.
points: How many updates you missed.
What kind of change each line is.
Got it: it won't show again, on any of your devices.

admin.label: Owner / admin
admin.blurb: The change log, admins, publishing updates, database updates and keeping this guide current.

slides.title: What the owner looks after
diagram: Any browser, or the home-screen app
dayforge.mkcworkspace.com on Vercel, built from GitHub: mkp-tools › dayforge
Sign-in, your data, private file storage
slides.text: Admins are the accounts on the admin list. The first account ever created is the first admin. Admins get ⋮ › Admin and the admin notes in What's new.

slides.title: The change log
slides.text: ⋮ › Admin › Change log has every update from launch to today. Every change lists each code change automatically, so nothing is missed.
points: Change log, Every change, Admins.
Newest or oldest first.
Everything, for everyone, or admin-only.
Download the whole history as CSV or JSON.

slides.title: Admins
slides.text: Add or remove admins by email. They need a DayForge account first, and the last admin can't be removed.
points: An admin and when they became one.
Their DayForge sign-in email.
Add admin.

slides.title: Account and sign-in
slides.text: Change the email or password from ⋮ › Account settings. Once your account exists, switch off “Allow new users to sign up” in Supabase › Authentication › Sign In / Providers.
points: New email: a confirmation link finishes the change.
New password: leave blank to keep the current one.

slides.title: Publishing an update
diagram: Usually within a minute or two
slides.text: If a release goes wrong, Vercel › Deployments › Instant Rollback puts the last good version back. Your data in Supabase isn't affected.

slides.title: Database updates
slides.text: Some features need a one-time database change, shipped as numbered files in dayforge/supabase/migrations. Run each one once, in order. Note labels need 008_note_labels.sql; admin roles need 009_admin_roles.sql.

slides.title: This guide keeps itself current
diagram: An automatic GitHub job rebuilds the guide and this tour
Add a release to dayforge/CHANGELOG.md. [Admins] lines reach admins only
slides.text: Each person sees new releases once, as What's new. If a button the guide points at is renamed or removed, the job stops and GitHub emails you, so the guide never quietly goes out of date.
